title: Vehicles
summary: How to read a tire size and the right pressure, battery terms, the safe jump-start order, fluid colours and rules, warning-light colours and OBD-II code letters. It also covers fuel storage, siphoning safety, and what not to do with airbags and electric-vehicle high-voltage parts.

steps.text: Find your topic in the headings. Check the owner's manual and the door-post placard first, because they override any general rule here.
Before touching a battery, fuel or fluid, read the safety lines in that section.
Match fluids, tire pressure and battery group to the manual, not to colour or habit.
steps.warn: Do not mix DOT 5 brake fluid with other types, and never siphon fuel by mouth.

steps.text: Leave airbags and high-voltage EV parts alone unless you have the vehicle's service procedure.
steps.warn: Orange cables carry high voltage. A damaged EV battery can catch fire days later.

notes:
## Read a tire: 215/65R16 98H
| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 215 | Section width in millimetres (USTMA) |
| 65 | Aspect ratio: sidewall height is 65 % of the width, so about 140 mm here (USTMA) |
| R | Radial construction (USTMA) |
| 16 | Rim diameter in inches (USTMA) |
| 98 | Load index. 98 means 750 kg per tire. 91 is 615 kg, 95 is 690 kg, 100 is 800 kg (Continental) |
| H | Speed symbol: 210 km/h (130 mph). T is 190 km/h, V is 240 km/h (USTMA) |

A leading **P** means passenger tire, **LT** means light truck (USTMA). The last four digits of the DOT code give the build week and year, so 0309 is week 3 of 2009 (USTMA).

**Pressure:** use the placard on the door edge, door post, glove box or fuel door, not the number on the tire. The tire number is its maximum (USTMA). Front and rear can differ. Check cold, meaning parked 3 hours or driven under 1.6 km (1 mile). Check monthly, spare included. Never bleed a hot tire. Tires lose 1 to 2 psi a month (USTMA).

## Battery terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| CCA | Amps a new, fully charged 12 V battery gives for 30 s at -18 °C (0 °F) without falling below 7.2 V (Stryten) |
| CA | Same test at 0 °C (32 °F) (Stryten) |
| Reserve capacity | Minutes at 25 A until 10.5 V, at 27 °C (80 °F) (Stryten) |
| Group size | BCI number for case size, terminal position and polarity, such as 24F, 35 or H6. Batteries in one group match in size within 2 mm (Stryten, BCI) |

Charging makes hydrogen, explosive at 4.1 to 72 % in air. Acid in an eye or on skin needs flushing with water for at least 30 minutes (CCOHS).

## Jump-start order
1. Do not jump a frozen or low-electrolyte battery. Use 12 V only, wear eye protection, keep flames and sparks away (Kia).
2. Red clamp to the **dead** battery **+**.
3. Other red clamp to the booster **+**.
4. Black clamp to the booster **-**.
5. Last black clamp to bare metal on the dead vehicle, **away from the battery**, at the marked point if the manual shows one (Honda, Kia).
6. Start the booster and raise its revs slightly, then start the dead vehicle. Remove clamps in reverse order (Honda).

**Why:** the battery gives off hydrogen, and the last connection makes a spark. Make it far from the battery (Kia). Joining the two negative posts directly can overheat and crack the dead battery (Kia). Never let clamp ends touch (Honda, Kia).

## Fluids
| Fluid | Colour and type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| Coolant | Green (older), red or orange, yellow, sometimes purple (AAA) | Colour does not show the type. Follow the manual. Do not mix types. Never open the radiator cap hot (AAA) |
| Brake fluid | DOT 3 and 4 clear to amber. DOT 5 silicone light purple (AAA) | **Never mix DOT 5 with DOT 3, 4 or 5.1** (Liqui Moly). Safest: mix no grades, and use the one your manual names. Dark brown or black: replace (AAA). Keep off paint (AAA) |
| Automatic transmission fluid | New is red or pink (AAA). CVT fluid has no standard colour (Castrol) | Dexron (GM) and Mercon (Ford) are common, but many makers specify their own (Castrol, AAA). A CVT needs CVT fluid (Castrol). Dark, milky or burnt: have it checked (AAA) |
| Power steering | Varies | Some use ATF, many need their own fluid. Check the manual. Buzzing at slow turns can mean low fluid (AAA) |

## Warning lights
| Colour | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Red | Possible serious fault. Pull over when safe. Oil pressure and coolant lights mean "Do not drive" (VW Canada). Do not start a trip with one on (National Highways) |
| Amber | Needs attention or service soon (VW Canada, AAA). Advisory (National Highways) |
| Green, blue, white | Information. A blue temperature light means the engine is still cold (VW Canada, AAA) |

Colours vary by maker. Your owner's manual rules (VW Canada).

## OBD-II codes (1996 and newer)
Example P0300: **P** powertrain, **B** body, **C** chassis, **U** network. Second digit, for P codes: 0 or 2 generic, 1 maker-specific, 3 either; for B, C and U codes: 0 generic, 1 or 2 maker-specific, 3 reserved. Third digit (P codes): 0 fuel, air and auxiliary emissions, 1-2 fuel and air, 3 ignition or misfire, 4 emission controls, 5 speed and idle, 6 computer, 7-9 transmission, A hybrid. Last two digits: the fault. The check-engine light comes on for emissions faults. Some makers vary from the generic meaning, so verify (MDE).

## Fuel and siphoning
- Gasoline can start to degrade in 30 days. Buy about a month's worth. Up to 10 % ethanol is fine in small engines, E15 is not (Briggs). Add stabiliser before filling the can. The maker claims up to 24 months (Briggs).
- Diesel: limit storage to about six months. Use an algaecide or fungicide additive in warm months (Penn State).
- Gasoline vapour ignites from a spark in any weather: flash point -43 °C, explosive at 1.4 to 7.6 % in air (NIOSH).
- **Never siphon by mouth.** A tiny amount in the lungs can cause pneumonia, coma or death (Poison Control).
- If swallowed or inhaled, call a poison centre: Canada 1-844-764-7669 (1-844-POISON-X; Quebec 1-800-463-5060), US 1-800-222-1222 (Health Canada, Poison Control). Do not induce vomiting unless told to. Move to fresh air if fumes were breathed (MedlinePlus). No poison centre: see [When no help is coming](#ref/reference_vehicles/when_no_help_is_coming).

## Airbags and EV high voltage
- Before any airbag work, disconnect the battery and wait at least 10 minutes. Times vary by maker (Subaru).
- Store a module flat, cover up, nothing on top, below 93 °C (200 °F). 149 °C (300 °F) can set it off (Subaru).
- Never measure a module's resistance. Never put yourself or test gear between module and seat. Never repair SRS wiring (Subaru).
- Never bin a live module (Subaru, Saab). Treat a deployed one as live. Wear gloves and eye protection (Saab, Subaru).
- **Orange cables are high voltage.** Never cut orange, yellow or blue cabling. Never touch damaged or wet HV parts (Nebraska DOT).
- A damaged EV battery can ignite days later. Store the vehicle outdoors, 15 m (50 ft) from buildings. Tow on a flatbed (Nebraska DOT).

**Get professional help** for brakes, steering, airbags and any high-voltage work.

## When no help is coming

**Fuel swallowed or breathed**
- Do not make the person vomit. Rinse the mouth. If fully alert, give one small glass of water, 100 to 200 mL (3 to 7 fl oz). No milk or other fatty drinks (Tox Info Suisse). Breathed it: fresh air (MedlinePlus).
- Skin: remove soaked clothing, wash with soapy water. Eyes: rinse 10 to 15 minutes (Tox Info Suisse).
- The danger is fuel reaching the lungs. Coughing, choking or vomiting raises the risk, and a tiny amount can be serious (Poison Control).
- Watch for cough, chest pain, fever and trouble breathing. Lung changes can show within 6 hours (Poison Control) and can start up to 3 days later (Tox Info Suisse).
- Serious: a cough that will not stop, breathing trouble, collapse, seizures, reduced alertness (Tox Info Suisse, MedlinePlus). There is no antidote for fuel in the lungs: care is support and close watching (CanadiEM).

**Brakes**
- Never drive with the red brake light on or the fluid below MIN. The brakes can fail completely (Mazda, Nissan).
- Minimum checks: the light goes out after starting, the fluid sits between the marks, and the parking brake is fully released. Low fluid or a fault can mean weaker braking: you may have to press harder, and the car may take longer to stop (Mazda, Nissan).
- Brake dust from older or replacement pads may contain asbestos. Wet parts with a fine mist before anything else, wipe clean with a cloth and seal the cloth in a bag for disposal, never dry-brush (OSHA brakes).

**Airbags**
- Disconnect the battery and wait 10 minutes. Never measure a module's resistance, put yourself or test gear between module and seat, or repair yellow SRS wiring (Subaru).
- Never discard a live module. A deployed dual-stage one may still be live (Saab). Wear gloves and eye protection with any deployed module (Subaru).
- Minimum check: the airbag light comes on about 3 seconds, then goes out. If it stays on or never lights, the system has a fault (Subaru).

**High voltage**
- Never cut orange, yellow or blue cabling. Never touch damaged or submerged high-voltage cables or parts (Nebraska DOT).
- Crashed EV: ignition off, keys 6 m away, wheels chocked, stay uphill and upwind. The battery can ignite days later. Keep it 15 m from buildings and tow on a flatbed only (Nebraska DOT).
